title: Q1 • Distance from Axis Examination Trap
prompt:
The perpendicular distance of the point $P(-4, -7)$ from the $y$-axis is:

(A) 4 units
(B) -4 units
(C) 7 units
(D) -7 units
solution:
Correct Answer: (A) 4 units

• The perpendicular distance of any point $(x, y)$ from the $y$-axis is given by the absolute value of its abscissa: $|x|$.
• Here, abscissa $x = -4$, so the perpendicular distance is $|-4| = \mathbf{4\text{ units}}$.
• Distance is a physical geometric measure and cannot be negative.
markingScheme: 1.0 mark: Correct option (A) identified with reasoning that distance to y-axis is |x| = |-4| = 4 units.
examinerTip: 🚨 Classic Trap: Over 40% of students write -4 or 7. Distance from y-axis is horizontal (|x|), and distance can never be negative.

title: Q2 • Quadrant Sign Inversion Problem
prompt:
If $a < 0$ and $b > 0$, then the point $Q(-a, -b)$ lies in:

(A) Quadrant I
(B) Quadrant II
(C) Quadrant III
(D) Quadrant IV
solution:
Correct Answer: (D) Quadrant IV

• Given $a < 0$ (negative), so the $x$-coordinate is $-a = -(\text{negative}) > 0$ (positive).
• Given $b > 0$ (positive), so the $y$-coordinate is $-b = -(\text{positive}) < 0$ (negative).
• A point with coordinates $(+, -)$ lies in Quadrant IV.
markingScheme: 1.0 mark: Correct option (D) selected after analyzing signs of -a (> 0) and -b (< 0).
examinerTip: 🚨 Tip: Don't see a minus sign and jump to 'negative'. If a is already negative, -a is positive!

title: Q3 • Assertion-Reasoning (Points on Coordinate Axes)
prompt:
Direction: In the question below, a statement of Assertion (A) is followed by a statement of Reason (R). Choose the correct option.

Assertion (A): The point $M(0, -5)$ does not lie in any quadrant.
Reason (R): Any point whose abscissa is zero lies strictly on the $y$-axis, and the coordinate axes do not belong to any quadrant.
options: (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
(B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
(C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
(D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
solution:
Correct Answer: (A)

• Assertion (A) is true: Since the $x$-coordinate is $0$, point $M(0, -5)$ lies on the negative $y$-axis, not in any quadrant.
• Reason (R) is true: By definition, points on the axes separate the quadrants and do not belong to Quadrants I, II, III, or IV.
• Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A).
markingScheme: 1.0 mark: Correct option (A) identified with valid conceptual reasoning.
examinerTip: 🚨 CBSE Rule: Quadrants are open geometric sets bounded by the axes. The axes themselves are boundary lines, not part of any quadrant.

title: Q4 • Identification of Coordinates and Quadrants
prompt:
Write the quadrant or axis on which each of the following points lies:
(i) $A(-3, 5)$
(ii) $B(4, -2)$
(iii) $C(-6, 0)$
(iv) $D(0, 7)$
solution:
• (i) Point $A(-3, 5)$: $x < 0, y > 0 \implies$ Quadrant II. [0.5 mark]
• (ii) Point $B(4, -2)$: $x > 0, y < 0 \implies$ Quadrant IV. [0.5 mark]
• (iii) Point $C(-6, 0)$: Since $y = 0$ and $x < 0 \implies$ Negative $x$-axis. [0.5 mark]
• (iv) Point $D(0, 7)$: Since $x = 0$ and $y > 0 \implies$ Positive $y$-axis. [0.5 mark]
markingScheme: 0.5 mark for each correct location precisely specified.
examinerTip: 🚨 Note: For (iii) and (iv), simply writing 'x-axis' or 'y-axis' is acceptable, but specifying 'negative x-axis' demonstrates top-tier precision.

title: Q5 • Perpendicular Projections & Coordinate Calculation
prompt:
From a point $P(-3, 4)$, perpendiculars $PM$ and $PN$ are drawn to the $x$-axis and $y$-axis respectively.
(a) State the coordinates of points $M$ and $N$. [1 Mark]
(b) Find the area of the rectangle $OMPN$, where $O$ is the origin. [1 Mark]
solution:
(a) Coordinates of $M$ and $N$:
• Foot of perpendicular on $x$-axis has $y = 0$, so $\mathbf{M(-3, 0)}$.
• Foot of perpendicular on $y$-axis has $x = 0$, so $\mathbf{N(0, 4)}$. [1.0 mark]

(b) Area of Rectangle $OMPN$:
• Length along $x$-axis: $OM = |-3| = 3$ units.
• Breadth along $y$-axis: $ON = |4| = 4$ units.
• $\text{Area} = OM \times ON = 3 \times 4 = \mathbf{12\text{ sq units}}$. [1.0 mark]
markingScheme: 0.5 mark for M(-3, 0) and 0.5 mark for N(0, 4).
1.0 mark for correctly calculating area = 3 × 4 = 12 sq units.
examinerTip: 🚨 Reminder: Units must be written as 'sq units' for coordinate area questions.

title: Q6 • Mirror Reflections Across Axes & Origin
prompt:
Let point $A$ have coordinates $(-4, 3)$.
(a) Write the coordinates of point $B$, which is the reflection of $A$ in the $x$-axis. [1 Mark]
(b) Write the coordinates of point $C$, which is the reflection of $A$ in the $y$-axis. [1 Mark]
(c) Write the coordinates of point $D$, which is the reflection of $A$ in the Origin $(0, 0)$. Also state the shape formed by joining $A, B, C, D$. [1 Mark]
solution:
(a) Reflection in $x$-axis ($B$):
In $x$-axis reflection, $x$ remains the same and $y$ flips sign:
$$\mathbf{B(-4, -3)}$$ [1.0 mark]

(b) Reflection in $y$-axis ($C$):
In $y$-axis reflection, $y$ remains the same and $x$ flips sign:
$$\mathbf{C(4, 3)}$$ [1.0 mark]

(c) Reflection in Origin ($D$) & Shape:
In Origin reflection, both coordinates flip sign:
$$\mathbf{D(4, -3)}$$
• Shape: Connecting $A(-4, 3)$, $C(4, 3)$, $D(4, -3)$, $B(-4, -3)$ forms a Rectangle (horizontal sides length 8 units, vertical sides length 6 units). [1.0 mark]
markingScheme: 0.5 mark for D(4, -3) and 0.5 mark for naming the shape Rectangle.
examinerTip: 🚨 Quick Check: Reflection in origin of A(-4, 3) is D(4, -3), which is diametrically opposite through (0, 0).

title: Q7 • Geometric Figure Synthesis on Coordinate Grid
prompt:
Three vertices of a parallelogram $PQRS$ are $P(-2, 2)$, $Q(3, 2)$, and $R(1, -2)$.
(a) Plot or calculate the coordinates of the fourth vertex $S$. [1.5 Marks]
(b) Calculate the area of the parallelogram $PQRS$. [1.5 Marks]
solution:
(a) Finding Coordinates of Vertex $S$:
• Side $PQ$ is horizontal because $y_P = y_Q = 2$.
Length $PQ = 3 - (-2) = 5$ units.
• Opposite side $SR$ must also be horizontal, parallel to $PQ$, and of length $5$ units.
Since $R$ is at $(1, -2)$, its ordinate is $-2$, so $y_S = -2$.
To match the orientation ($P$ is 5 units left of $Q$), $S$ must be 5 units left of $R$:
$$x_S = x_R - 5 = 1 - 5 = -4$$
Hence, $\mathbf{S(-4, -2)}$. [1.5 marks]

(b) Area of Parallelogram:
$$\text{Area} = \text{Base} \times \text{Height}$$
• $\text{Base} = PQ = 5$ units.
• $\text{Height} = \text{Vertical distance between } y=2 \text{ and } y=-2$:
$$\text{Height} = 2 - (-2) = 4\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Area} = 5 \times 4 = \mathbf{20\text{ sq units}}$$ [1.5 marks]
markingScheme: 1.5 marks: Stating horizontal side length PQ = 5 and determining S(-4, -2).
1.5 marks: Calculating vertical height = 4 units and area = 5 × 4 = 20 sq units.
examinerTip: 🚨 Concept Tip: Parallelogram area is NOT base × slant side! It is strictly base × perpendicular height.

title: Q8 • Long Answer HOTS: Triangle Area & Collinearity
prompt:
Consider points on a Cartesian coordinate grid:

Part (a): Points $A(1, 2)$, $B(5, 2)$, and $C(3, 6)$ are plotted on graph paper.
(i) Plot/describe the positions of the points and prove that $\Delta ABC$ is an isosceles triangle.
(ii) Calculate the exact area of $\Delta ABC$. [3 Marks]

Part (b): Determine whether the points $K(-1, -1)$, $L(2, 3)$, and $M(5, 7)$ are collinear using coordinate geometry distance/slope reasoning. [2 Marks]
solution:
Part (a) Solution:
1. Side $AB$ lies on the horizontal line $y = 2$.
Length $AB = |5 - 1| = 4$ units. [0.5 mark]
2. The midpoint of base $AB$ is $D\left(\frac{1+5}{2}, 2\right) = D(3, 2)$.
3. Vertex $C(3, 6)$ has $x$-coordinate $3$, which lies directly on the perpendicular bisector $x = 3$ of $AB$.
• Distance $AD = |3 - 1| = 2$, Height $CD = |6 - 2| = 4$.
• By Pythagoras theorem in $\Delta ADC$: $AC = \sqrt{AD^2 + CD^2} = \sqrt{2^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{20}$.
• In $\Delta BDC$: $BC = \sqrt{BD^2 + CD^2} = \sqrt{2^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{20}$.
Since $AC = BC = \sqrt{20}$, $\mathbf{\Delta ABC\text{ is an isosceles triangle}}$. [1.5 marks]

4. Area of $\Delta ABC$:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{Base} \times \text{Height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 4 = \mathbf{8\text{ sq units}}$$ [1.0 mark]

---

Part (b) Solution:
Points are collinear if the slope between consecutive pairs is identical:
• Slope of $KL = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1} = \frac{3 - (-1)}{2 - (-1)} = \frac{4}{3}$. [0.5 mark]
• Slope of $LM = \frac{7 - 3}{5 - 2} = \frac{4}{3}$. [0.5 mark]
Since $\text{Slope}(KL) = \text{Slope}(LM)$ and point $L$ is common to both segments, points $K, L, M$ lie on the same straight line.
Hence, $\mathbf{K, L, M\text{ are collinear}}$. [1.0 mark]
markingScheme: 1.0 mark: Finding base length AB = 4 units.
1.0 mark: Proving AC = BC = √20 using Pythagoras theorem to confirm isosceles triangle.
1.0 mark: Finding slope of KL = 4/3 and slope of LM = 4/3.
1.0 mark: Stating conclusive collinearity proof due to common point L.
examinerTip: 🚨 CBSE Presentation: In Class 9, proving collinearity using slopes or segment distance comparisons is awarded full 2 marks.

title: Q9 • Section E: Case-Based Integrated Study
prompt:
CASE STUDY: Smart City Logistics & Drone Navigation

A smart logistics center in Chandigarh uses an automated delivery drone network. The municipal delivery hub is situated at the reference Origin $O(0, 0)$. Two main perpendicular avenues represent the $x$-axis (East-West Highway) and $y$-axis (North-South Boulevard). All coordinates are specified in kilometers from the central hub.

• Distribution Center 1 is located at $P(3, 4)$ (3 km East, 4 km North).
• Distribution Center 2 is located at $Q(-3, 4)$ (3 km West, 4 km North).
• Residential Depot is located at $R(-3, -2)$ (3 km West, 2 km South).

Based on this coordinate framework, answer the following:

(i) Name the quadrants in which Distribution Center 1 and Residential Depot $R$ are situated. [1 Mark]

(ii) What is the geometric relationship between the positions of Distribution Center 1 ($P$) and Distribution Center 2 ($Q$)? [1 Mark]

(iii) To build a closed delivery perimeter, a fourth station $S$ is planned such that $PQRS$ forms a perfect rectangle. Determine the coordinates of Station $S$ and find the total area enclosed within the flight perimeter $PQRS$.
[OR]
If a drone flies straight from Distribution Center 1 ($P(3, 4)$) to the East-West Highway ($x$-axis) along the shortest perpendicular path, state the coordinates of its landing point on the highway and the distance flown. [2 Marks]
solution:
(i) Quadrants of $P$ and $R$:
• $P(3, 4)$: $x > 0, y > 0 \implies$ Quadrant I. [0.5 mark]
• $R(-3, -2)$: $x < 0, y < 0 \implies$ Quadrant III. [0.5 mark]

(ii) Geometric Relationship between $P(3, 4)$ and $Q(-3, 4)$:
• Points $P(3, 4)$ and $Q(-3, 4)$ are reflections of each other across the $y$-axis (North-South Boulevard).
• They lie along the horizontal line $y = 4$ and are symmetric with respect to the vertical axis. [1.0 mark]

(iii) Primary Option (Station $S$ & Area):
• Length $PQ = 3 - (-3) = 6$ km along $y = 4$.
• Vertical breadth $QR = 4 - (-2) = 6$ km along $x = -3$.
• To complete the rectangle (which is actually a square since length = breadth = 6 km), station $S$ must have:
$$x_S = x_P = 3, \quad y_S = y_R = -2 \implies \mathbf{S(3, -2)}$$ [1.0 mark]
• $\text{Flight Perimeter Area} = 6\text{ km} \times 6\text{ km} = \mathbf{36\text{ sq km}}$. [1.0 mark]

[OR] Internal Choice Option:
• Shortest path from $P(3, 4)$ to $x$-axis is the perpendicular dropped to $y = 0$.
• Landing point coordinates: $\mathbf{(3, 0)}$. [1.0 mark]
• Distance flown $= |y| = |4| = \mathbf{4\text{ km}}$. [1.0 mark]
markingScheme: 0.5 mark for Quadrant I and 0.5 mark for Quadrant III.
1.0 mark for stating reflection across the y-axis (or line y = 4 with y-axis symmetry).
2.0 marks: [Main Option] Finding S(3, -2) [1m] and Area = 36 sq km [1m]. OR [Choice Option] Finding landing point (3, 0) [1m] and distance = 4 km [1m].
examinerTip: 🚨 CBSE Case Study Tip: Always include units (km, sq km) in real-world case study problems to avoid losing fractional presentation marks.
